title: Practice: Development of the Atomic Model

questions.stem: What did Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment demonstrate about atomic structure?

options.text: Atoms contain electrons embedded in a positive sphere
Atoms are mostly empty space with a small, dense, positive nucleus
Electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels
Atoms are solid, indivisible spheres

questions.explanation: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil (showing atoms are mostly empty space), some were deflected (showing a positive centre repelling the positive alpha particles), and very few bounced back (showing the nucleus is small and dense). This disproved Thomson's plum pudding model.

questions.stem: In Rutherford's experiment, a very small number of alpha particles bounced back towards the source. What does this specific observation tell us?

options.text: Electrons have a negative charge
The atom is mostly empty space
The nucleus is very small but contains most of the atom's mass
Atoms contain neutrons

questions.explanation: Alpha particles bouncing back indicates they hit something very dense and positively charged (like charges repel). The fact that very few bounced back shows the nucleus is extremely small compared to the atom. For an alpha particle to reverse direction, the nucleus must be massive enough to repel it. Neutrons were discovered later by Chadwick.

questions.stem: Which model of the atom did Thomson propose?

options.text: The nuclear model with orbiting electrons
The solid sphere model with no internal structure
The plum pudding model with electrons embedded in positive charge
The electron shell model with fixed energy levels

questions.explanation: Thomson proposed the plum pudding model after discovering the electron. In this model, the atom was a sphere of positive charge with negative electrons embedded throughout it, like plums in a pudding. This model was later disproved by Rutherford's scattering experiment. Dalton proposed the solid sphere model.

questions.stem: Why was Bohr's model of the atom an improvement on Rutherford's model?

options.text: Bohr discovered the neutron
Bohr showed that the atom was mostly empty space
Bohr proposed that electrons orbit in fixed energy levels, not just anywhere
Bohr proved that the nucleus was positively charged

questions.explanation: Rutherford's model had electrons orbiting the nucleus but did not explain why they didn't spiral into it. Bohr improved the model by proposing that electrons occupy fixed energy levels (shells) at specific distances from the nucleus. This explained the emission spectra of elements. Chadwick later discovered the neutron.

questions.stem: The atomic model has changed over time. Which sequence correctly shows the order of model development?

options.text: Plum pudding → Solid sphere → Nuclear model → Bohr model
Solid sphere → Nuclear model → Plum pudding → Bohr model
Solid sphere → Plum pudding → Nuclear model → Bohr model
Nuclear model → Solid sphere → Plum pudding → Bohr model

questions.explanation: The correct order is: Dalton's solid sphere model (early 1800s) → Thomson's plum pudding model (1897, after discovering electrons) → Rutherford's nuclear model (1911, from alpha scattering) → Bohr's model with electron shells (1913). Each new model built on or corrected the previous one based on new experimental evidence.
